note: Utqiagvik (Point Barrow), north Alaska: the Birnirk and early Thule homeland, whales and driftwood both abundant
Qikiqtaruk (Herschel Island), Yukon coast: the Washout site (NjVi-2), one of the two western sites Friesen and Arnold redated in 2008
Cape Parry, Amundsen Gulf: the corridor any eastward migration had to pass
Kugaaruk and Committee Bay, at the head of the Gulf of Boothia
Naujaat (Repulse Bay): Mathiassen's Naujan, the type site of the Thule culture in the central Arctic
Iglulik and northern Foxe Basin: walrus and bowhead, and the raised beaches that carry the whole sequence
Skraeling Island, Alexandra Fiord, Ellesmere Island: Early Thule houses of the Ruin Island phase, holding Norse iron, chain mail and cloth
Etah and Inglefield Land, northwest Greenland: the Thule reach the Greenland shore and meet the Norse trade from the south
